title: Nightly snapshot spans every location with no user location filter
refs: SV-8667 (WIP spec v24 per Chris Ward 2026-08-19; Story 11 S11-R4; Story 2 S2-R1; S11-R7 corrected - the snapshot is read via the "as of" date)
preconds:
1. Open service work orders exist at two or more different locations.
2. An Invoiced (or Paid/Declined) work order and a part-sale work order also exist.
3. You can open the Work In Progress report and set its "as of" date..
steps:
1. On the report, set the "as of" date to a day that has a snapshot.
2. Check that open service work orders from EVERY location are present.
3. Look for the Invoiced/Paid/Declined work order and the part-sale work order.
expected:
1. The captured set uses the same service-type and open-status conditions as the report (service work orders in Estimate, Approved, In Progress, Review, or Complete).
2. The capture spans every location - there is no user-selected-location filter.
3. Invoiced, Paid and Declined work orders and part-sale work orders are not captured.

Note for the tester: you CAN check this from the report. The "as of" read has no user-selected-location filter - it spans every location. Confirm open service work orders from every location appear, and that Invoiced, Paid, Declined and part-sale work orders do not.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8582 and story SV-8667 (WIP Story 11), and the Work In Progress report specification version 28 (S11-R4, S2-R1), as pinned and answered by Chris Ward on 19 August 2026, recorded in his answers in this file: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilalmuzamil-sketch/Manual-test-Cases/claude/slack-session-0sxnd9/build/report-suite/chris-answers-2026-08-19/WIP-CHRIS-RULINGS-2026-08-19.md.
This corrects the older wording (specification version 22), which said nothing in the report reads the snapshot back. Chris Ward confirmed on 19 August 2026 that the "as of" date reconstructs a past day from the snapshot, so that newest source is followed here.
Last checked against build v3.8-d0e135e on 8/19/2026.
Re-checked against the live specification on 28 August 2026: every requirement this case cites was read again in the live version and the behaviour above still matches it, so only the version cited above was updated.

AUTOMATION: READY
